sections.heading: Our Process for Flat Roof Installation and Repair in East Orange, NJ

c.v: Newark Quality Roofing measures the slope, locates the ponding, and inspects the deck and the existing membrane before specifying a flat-roof scope.

c.v: Newark Quality Roofing matches the flat roof to one of three membrane systems — EPDM rubber, TPO thermoplastic, or modified bitumen — and corrects the slope with tapered insulation toward the drains.

runs.v: Local climate shapes the material selection, proper insulation improves a flat roof's energy efficiency, and white TPO reflects solar radiation to reduce the cooling load on a sun-exposed roof. sections.heading: Choosing Flat Roofing Materials: EPDM vs. TPO vs. Modified Bitumen

c.v: Each membrane suits a different building.

runs.v: Commercial flat roofing includes EPDM, TPO, and modified bitumen: TPO is known for its energy efficiency and UV resistance, single-ply membranes reflect heat and tolerate brief ponding better than asphalt-based roofs, EPDM gives durable single-ply coverage on commercial buildings for 15 to 25 years, and modified bitumen resists puncture under heavy rooftop traffic. Flat roof types also differ from the shingle roofs on the pitched sections of the same East Orange residential buildings: asphalt shingles are the most common roofing material in East Orange, architectural shingles last about 30 years when properly installed, and metal roofing systems can last 50 years or longer. Shingle roofs show age as granule loss and missing shingles; a flat roof shows it as blisters, open seams, and ponding. On pitched sections, complete roof replacements use GAF and Owens Corning shingle systems, both brands Newark Quality Roofing installs. A flat roof is mostly invisible from the street, so curb appeal matters less than drainage.

sections.heading: East Orange Roofing FAQs for Essex County Flat Roofs

faqs.q: Do I need a permit for a flat roof in East Orange, NJ?

runs.v: Not on a detached one- or two-family home, where even a full roof replacement of the roof covering is ordinary maintenance under N.J.A.C. 5:23-2.7 and needs no permit. On a commercial, multi-family, or attached East Orange building, the large majority of the city's stock, repairing more than 25% of the total roof area in a 12-month period requires a permit; that threshold is the 25% rule.

faqs.q: Which flat-roof membrane is best for an East Orange apartment building?

runs.v: It depends on the roof: white TPO for a sun-exposed roof, EPDM for durable single-ply coverage, modified bitumen under heavy rooftop traffic. A Newark Quality Roofing assessment matches the membrane to each building's use, load, and drainage.

faqs.q: Can a new flat roof go over the existing layers on my East Orange building?

runs.v: Only when the existing roof has fewer than two layers, the insulation tests dry, and the deck carries the added weight. N.J.A.C. 5:23-6.4 requires a full tear-off when the roof is water-soaked or already carries 2 or more applications, which a core sample often finds on pre-war East Orange walk-ups.

faqs.q: Why does water pond on my East Orange flat roof, and is it a problem?

runs.v: Water ponds when the slope drops below ¼ inch per foot, and ponding water remaining more than 48 hours counts as a defect that breaks down membrane seams, per the NRCA and ARMA. Tapered insulation toward the drains corrects the slope.

faqs.q: How do you schedule flat-roof work on an occupied East Orange rental building?

runs.v: The crew sets the access, staging, and delivery plan before the start date, coordinates any roof hatch inside a unit with the owner under New Jersey's advance-notice rules, and contains tear-off debris above occupied floors.
